Feature switches in Miroir: where they stand and what blocks profiles

Long image

A

Answer

Miroir has seven kinds of switch, and only process capabilities behave like a switch system. Even those are declared in seven places, gate without unloading, and freeze at process start. A plain runtime needs one declaration per switch that joins hide, refuse and load. Gradual enablement also needs values that change after start.

  1. Adding one capability touches three ML schema copies, two code sites, a fail-closed constant and a hand-written doc table.1
  2. Only ai ties its switch to a lazy chunk; designerTools hides menus but its route still renders, and mcp off still imports miroir-mcp.
  3. Viewing a report instance renders TypedValueObjectEditor, so a plain runtime would still load Formik and the ML editor stack.
  4. Values are global booleans read once at start, while a dark launch needs scopes, states and change without restart.

Applies toSurvey of _integration at c61c7242026-10-25no decision takenbundle savings not measured

1

Which kinds of switch exist today?

The word "feature" covers seven mechanisms with different owners and lifetimes. Only the first three decide what code a process carries.

KindWho sets itWhen it can changeExample
Load boundarythe code, by dynamic import()on first use11 lazy routes in PageDispatcher.tsx, ensureYamlParser()
Build profilethe build, by define or aliasper buildMIROIR_IS_SANDBOX, nodeStoreStub.js
Process capabilitythe environment featuresFrozenat process startai, mcp, designerTools
Access rightAdmin MiroirRightLiveat runtimedesigner tools with authentication on
Application modeSelfApplication rowLiveat runtimeversioningMode
UI togglesessionStorageper tabshowModelTools, showDebugInfo
Diagnosticenvironment variableat process startMIROIR_EVOLUTION_TRACE

UI toggles and diagnostics are not feature switches. The analysis lists them so the G6 decision excludes them explicitly.

2

How does a process capability travel from config to gate?

Diagram structure
  • environments/env.json envfile
  • miroir-env resolver resolver
  • getProcessCapabilities snapshot
  • GET /capabilities http
  • UI hides what is off ui
  • DomainController dc
  • FeatureUnavailable refuse
  • Lazy chunk (ai only) chunk
  • envfile → resolver · features
  • resolver → snapshot · MiroirConfigServer
  • snapshot → http · snapshot
  • http → ui · fetch
  • snapshot → dc · set
  • dc → refuse · assert
  • ui → chunk · ai on
  1. environments/env.json ↗

    Declares ai, mcp, agentBackend, agentModel, designerTools. Test environments declare none.

  2. getProcessCapabilities ↗

    Applies defaults and vetoes in code, once at start. The sandbox veto on ai works only because the sandbox computes its own snapshot.

  3. GET /capabilities ↗

    Serves the snapshot over HTTP, RestClientStub or Electron IPC. The UI keeps the copy fetched before login.

  4. FeatureUnavailable ↗

    assertProcessCapability refuses leftover actions with an Action2Error.

  5. Lazy chunk (ai only) ↗

    The only place where "off" also means "not loaded", written by hand twice.

4

Why is a plain runtime not a matter of turning switches off?

Diagram structure
  • Report instance page report
  • ReportSectionEntityInstance section
  • TypedValueObjectEditor tvoe
  • Formik context formik
  • ML element editor stack mlstack
  • Entry chunk entry
  • miroir-app-miroir deployment metamodel
  • miroir-core single bundle core
  • report → section · renders
  • section → tvoe · display
  • tvoe → formik · useFormikContext
  • tvoe → mlstack · imports
  • entry → metamodel · eager, 3.4 MB cap
  • entry → core · splitting off

Viewing code depends on editing code, and two bundling choices keep the editor in the eager path.

  1. TypedValueObjectEditor ↗

    11 modules render it, including instance display and report inputs. A plain runtime needs a read-only display module with a small interface.

  2. ML element editor stack ↗

    components/ValueObjectEditor/ holds 9189 lines of TSX.

  3. miroir-app-miroir deployment ↗

    The meta-model sits in the entry chunk, MiroirTest component test instances included.

  4. miroir-core single bundle ↗

    tsup with splitting: false inlines its own dynamic imports, so core editing logic cannot become a lazy chunk without a subpath entry or package split.

How much would a plain runtime save?

Nobody knows yet. The first measurement is a bundle report of the home page plus a report page, designer tools off versus on.

5

Where could a switch value come from?

Diagram structure
  • Build profile ceiling profile
  • Environment features env
  • Boot-time switches boot
  • Admin switch rows admin
  • Scoped value scoped
  • admin → scoped · user, app, share
  • boot → admin · opens Admin
  • env → boot · resolves
  • profile → env · bounds

A dark launch needs values that change after start and vary by scope. Admin data already does that for rights and application modes, but some switches decide what to load before Admin opens.

  1. Build profile ceiling ↗

    define constants per profile (runtime, platform, sandbox) let Rollup drop code. Without a ceiling rule, an environment could turn on code the build removed.

  2. Boot-time switches ↗

    Switches that choose chunks or stores must be known before Admin opens: the boot-order problem #321 settled for environments.

  3. Admin switch rows ↗

    Follows the MiroirRight and SelfApplication precedents: model data, editable at runtime, scoped.

Need for gradual enablementToday
Change without restartMissing"Restart the process after you edit flags"
Scope: user, role, application, share of usersPartialprocess-wide; only rights and application rows vary
States beyond on and off: dark, previewMissingbooleans
Owner and removal date per switchMissingnone; the features.cursor alias shows the cost
Audit of who turned it onMissingnone

4 sites, 3 different tests for Electron or sandbox
B7 test environments
test-* declare no features: ai and mcp off, designerTools on
B8 drifts
